name: Hospitality
headline: Connect the guest journey with the work behind it.
description: Hospitality website and workflow planning for clearer room discovery, inquiries and reception handoffs.
situation: A beautiful room page helps discovery, but guests also need clear availability, policies and a dependable next step.
plan: Clarify room information, amenities and booking or inquiry paths.
Map how a confirmed reservation reaches reception and who updates its status.
Separate real availability from inquiry-only experiences so guests never see a false promise.
questions: Who confirms a booking and handles changes?
How do reception and housekeeping share room status?
boundary: Booking engines, OTAs, payment providers and cancellation rules must be agreed before a live integration.

name: Restaurants & cafés
headline: Clearer orders. Calmer service.
description: Restaurant ordering and staff workflows built around accurate menus, confirmation and preparation handoffs.
situation: Menus, incoming questions and preparation queues often live in different places. Missing details turn into delays at the counter.
plan: Establish one accurate menu with availability and pricing rules.
Collect necessary delivery or collection details before confirmation.
Define who approves exceptions and how orders reach the preparation queue.
questions: What counts as a confirmed order?
boundary: Food orders, delivery promises and payments require reliable provider integrations. An AI response alone is never an order confirmation.

name: Clinic operations
headline: Give reception a shared view of the day.
description: Reception workflow planning for patient lookup, visit queues and payment records with clear privacy boundaries.
situation: A returning visit should not mean re-entering the same record. Reception needs a practical view without exposing unnecessary information.
plan: Map patient identification separately from visits and payments.
Define staff permissions and the minimum information each task requires.
Agree on privacy, retention, backups and access review before using real data.
questions: Which roles can view or change each record?
What data is genuinely needed at reception?
How will backups and access be checked?
boundary: Clinical decisions, regulated health records and compliance certification are outside this reception concept. Real deployment requires a separate security and privacy review.

name: Professional services
headline: Turn expertise into a clear reason to get in touch.
description: Service websites and inquiry workflows that help buyers understand expertise, scope and the next step.
situation: A referral may bring someone to your website, but the site still needs to explain whether you solve their particular problem.
plan: Organize pages around buyer needs, deliverables and evidence.
Explain your process and the information needed for a useful first discussion.
Qualify inquiries without forcing visitors through a long sales funnel.
questions: What makes an inquiry a good fit?
Which questions repeat before a project starts?
What evidence can you publish with permission?
boundary: Credentials, client names and results are included only when verified and approved for publication.

name: Startups & product teams
headline: Build the smallest useful version with a path forward.
description: Focused product planning, web experiences and internal tools for testing an early business workflow.
situation: An early product needs to prove a useful workflow before a large feature list becomes expensive to maintain.
plan: Choose one audience, one problem and a measurable completion event.
Prototype the riskiest interaction using realistic but non-sensitive sample data.
Document what is experimental, what is ready and what needs validation before launch.
questions: What is essential for the first complete workflow?
Who owns the product after handover?
boundary: A prototype is not automatically ready for customer data, payment processing or scale. Launch gates are explicit.
